title: KiTZ Mobile Trial Team [MTT]
summary:
The MTT study (KiTZ Mobile Trial Team study) aims to systematically investigate and characterize the logistical, medical-clinical, and psychological aspects of partial home care provided by a mobile treatment team in pediatric oncology.
The aim is to test the hypothesis that home visits in pediatric oncology are logistically feasible, generate high-quality medical data in terms of both quality and quantity, improve the quality of life of patients and families, and that reducing the burden of participating in clinical trials will result in more patients wanting to participate in such trials. This may enable more patients to access new drugs and, in the best case scenario, lead to faster knowledge gain for better treatment for future generations of patients.
Patients undergoing treatment for cancer at KiTZ Heidelberg with a compatible treatment protocol can participate in the study. An individualized visit schedule is created for these patients, in which selected hospital visits are replaced by home visits. During the visits, questionnaires are administered to assess the extent to which the quality of life of patients and their families has changed and what impact the home visits have on the families' daily routines. In addition, saliva samples are taken from patients at selected timepoints to measure the concentration of the hormone cortisol in their saliva as a marker for the biological stress level.
conditions: Clinical studies in pediatric oncology should better adress the needs of patients and families by implementing a mobile trial team.

interventions.name:
Patients with home visits
For these patients as many study or regular treatment visits are performed at the patient's home

At all visits (but not more frequent than every 4 weeks) the following data are collected:
1) Quality of life (patients and families) [questionnaires: PedsQL_4.0-Core-All_A

Patients without home visits
For these patients all study or regular treatment visits are performed at the hospital

Every 4 weeks the following data are collected:
1) Quality of life (patients and families) [questionnaires: PedsQL_4.0-Core-All_AU4.0_deu-DE, PedsQL-3.0-Cancer-All_AU3.0_deu-DE, P

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Oncological disease
- Treatment at the Hopp Children's Cancer Center (KiTZ) Heidelberg as part of a clinical trial (phase I/II/III) or guideline-based therapy with observation as part of a registry
- Treatment protocol classified as compatible with MTT participation (see below)
- Place of residence accessible by car within approximately 1 hour of KiTZ Heidelberg
- Written consent form from patients/parents
Exclusion criteria:
1) Before the first home visit is carried out, a home visit with a “safety and feasibility check” is carried out. For this purpose, the local conditions of the place of residence are recorded in a standardized manner in order to determine whether the planned treatment can be carried out safely. If the safety and feasibility check is not passed, the patient is excluded from the study. The following are necessary for a positive safety and feasibility check:
- A quiet place for patient treatment (e.g., own room)
- Adequate hygienic conditions
- Accessibility within approximately 1 hour's drive by car from KiTZ Heidelberg
- Adequate network reception for telephone communication with KiTZ
2) During one of the first 3 visits to the hospital, an unexpected complication arises that changes the risk assessment of the procedure to be performed.
3) Insufficient compliance with repeated absence of the patient when the mobile team arrives
4) Withdrawal of consent by the study participant or legal guardian
